subject: ISV certification and publisher redistribution paths
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>
To: OpenHarbor Partnerships <partners@openharbor.ai>, camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exploring redistribution options for OpenHarbor models with ISV partners

Hi Ravi / OpenHarbor team —

Thanks again for the demo last week. There was strong interest from a couple of ISV partners (consulting shop + vertical SaaS) to include your 2.7B conversational model as a redistributable artifact they can ship inside their appliance images. Before we set expectations, I wanted to outline the two broad paths we see and check what OpenHarbor is willing to consider:

1) Controlled redistribution: OpenHarbor provides weights access to Redwood under an addendum; Redwood manages a per-ISV redistribution process (escrow + per-license keys, quantization/distribution controls, audit logs).

2) Hosted-only: Model remains with OpenHarbor / Redwood Dedicated. ISVs integrate via API calls (no weights handed to ISVs).

Key asks from our partners: support for quantized redistributions (INT8/4-bit), clear attribution requirements, and an expedited certification that lets ISVs display an "OpenHarbor Certified on Redwood" badge.

Can you share any constraints around redistribution (embargo windows, forbid/allow transfer, escrow requirements), and whether you have a standard addendum you prefer? I’m looping Camila and Marcus to coordinate the commercial and engineering controls.

Attachments: partnership_faq_stub.pdf (overview)

Next step: If you’re open to discussing both options, can we schedule a 30-minute call this week?

Thanks,
Sergio
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Ravi Singh <ravi@openharbor.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>, camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 11:05:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring redistribution options for OpenHarbor models with ISV partners

Sergio —

Appreciate the clear framing. OpenHarbor's high-level view today: we are open to redistribution in principle but with safeguards. Our legal team typically requires:

- Per-ISV licensing addendum (we can start from our Redistribution Addendum).
- Escrow or controlled distribution: we need visibility into who holds the artifacts and auditable delivery records.
- No permanent re-licensing: ISVs can include the model in their product binaries only under an explicit time-limited license or under device-bound licensing.
- Attribution and model provenance must be preserved in any redistributed weights.
- Security evidence: SOC 2 report, KMS process (how keys are handled), and attestations for any party that will hold raw weights.

I attached a redline of our Redistribution Addendum (OH-redistribution-addendum-redline.docx). Two open items worth flagging:
- We prohibit third-party re-hosting (i.e., an ISV cannot put the model on a public registry).
- We prefer escrow over simple key-exchange for high-value models; escrow provider suggestions?

We can take the call Thursday 10am PT. Also looping Kate Hsu from Nimbus (they're an ISV considering integration) for initial product requirements.

—Ravi
OpenHarbor, Partner Ops
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>, Ravi Singh <ravi@openharbor.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 09:20:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring redistribution options for OpenHarbor models with ISV partners

Thanks Ravi — useful redline. Quick summary from our side and two pragmatic paths to keep momentum:

Path A — Redwood-managed redistribution (preferred for ISV portability):
- Redwood ingests publisher weights into a VPC-controlled artifact store.
- Per-ISV sealed license bundles generated; keys escrowed with a neutral escrow (we can propose two providers).
- Quantization pipeline runs within Redwood; we sign resulting artifacts and emit a provenance file.
- Auditable delivery report for OpenHarbor and the ISV.
- Certification: ISV passes a 3-step checklist (security checklist, runtime testset, UI attribution) to earn an "OpenHarbor Certified on Redwood" badge.

Path B — Hosted-only integration (lower legal friction):
- No weights leave Redwood/OpenHarbor. ISVs call a dedicated endpoint with higher QPS/throughput SLAs.
- Lower commercial complexity, but ISVs lose offline/offline-device use cases.

Action items we propose before the call:
1) Laura — can you prepare a commercial outline for a redistribution seat (rev share vs fixed fee) and a draft certification checklist?
2) Marcus — engineering: rough security/ingest checklist and candidate escrow vendors.
3) Ravi — any non-negotiable term line items you want us to prepare for the addendum redline.

I attached our draft ISV_cert_requirements_v0.2.pdf to show the certification flow.

If OpenHarbor is okay with Path A, we can run a short pilot with a single ISV to validate the flow (30–60 day timeline).

—Camila
Head of Publisher Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Maria Chen <maria.chen@consultsoft.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>, camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, ravi@openharbor.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 14:02:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring redistribution options for OpenHarbor models with ISV partners

Hi all — quick note from the ISV side (ConsultSoft). Our product team cares about two things: (1) being able to run quantized weights on-device (we use an appliance model), and (2) a clear process for re-certification after model patch updates (we can only ship if cert resilience is < 7 days).

If Redwood can guarantee a signed quantization artifact and an expedited re-cert flow for security patches, ConsultSoft can commit to a commercial pilot. We are comfortable with time-limited licenses bound to a device ID, and we’re open to rev-share if the economics are favorable.

We’d like to join the Thursday call if possible.

Thanks,
Maria Chen
VP Product, ConsultSoft
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>, camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, ravi@openharbor.ai
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 10:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring redistribution options for OpenHarbor models with ISV partners

Looping in the commercial/finance view after reading the redline. Top-level proposals:

- Pilot pricing: fixed intake fee (covers ingest, quantization, provenance signing) + a monthly redistribution seat fee. Recommend $12,500 intake + $2,500/mo seat.
- Revenue share for upstream publisher: start at 65/35 in favor of OpenHarbor for year 1, then revisit on adoption milestones.
- Escrow costs to be absorbed by the ISV for pilot (we can price and standardize for scale).
- Certification fee: one-time $5k technical validation; included in intake for a single pilot ISV.

Please note: any permanent redistribution into public registries is forbidden per OpenHarbor's redline. We need to capture that in our commercial template.

Related links: HubSpot record and the DocuSign addendum for records. I can draft the commercial term sheet after the call.

—Laura
Head of Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring redistribution options for OpenHarbor models with ISV partners — agreed pilot plan + next steps

Great discussion today — thanks everyone for the clarity. Quick recap and owners: 

1) Pilot path agreed: Path A (Redwood-managed redistribution) for a single ISV pilot (ConsultSoft).
   - Owner: Camila (publisher ops) + Marcus (ingest/quant)
   - Timeline: artifact ingest and signed quantized build within 21 days of PO.

2) Commercial terms (draft): intake fee $12.5k + $2.5k/mo seat + 65/35 rev share to OpenHarbor for year 1.
   - Owner: Laura to produce term sheet and DocuSign link.

3) Legal: OpenHarbor will finalize the redline to the Redistribution Addendum. DocuSign link requested for e-sign.

4) Security: Redwood to provide SOC 2 attest and write-up on key management and escrow vendor shortlist.

5) Certification: Redwood will publish an ISV checklist; ConsultSoft needs to complete runtime tests (target <7 days re-cert time).

Action items due: Laura (term sheet + DocuSign) by 2027-04-08; Marcus (vendor shortlist) by 2027-04-07; Camila (pilot runbook) by 2027-04-09.

Attachments: publisher_qa_matrix.xlsx (pilot acceptance criteria)

If there are no objections I’ll send the HubSpot update and attach the DocuSign once Laura produces the term sheet.

Thanks,
Sergio
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference
